gaps.text: In-line measurement of turbidity (optical density) of the stream with inline turbidity or optical-density sensor
In-line measurement of process temperature at the measurement point with temperature sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Fusion level: one model per method first, then a joined, block-scaled matrix, because variables from different methods are not equivalent. The NIR transmission path and the mid-IR ATR crystal must sit at the same flow-cell location and the data must be normalised to a common time step, since the two techniques sample different volumes. The fused model must beat the best single method on held-out runs, and each instrument keeps its own calibration and diagnostics.)
One measurement concept can cover both the clear and the more turbid stream state.

items.finding: The source says temperature sensitivity of OH bands is a severe drawback for aqueous NIR and MIR measurement, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: This could inform the measurement concept by supporting temperature control or temperature monitoring at the flow cell, and by prompting tests of how process temperature shifts affect the NIR/MIR signal.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a review of biopharmaceutical downstream processing, not dairy whey, and it discusses tempered sample holders rather than an in-line temperature sensor at a dairy process point.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E02 ¶12

items.finding: The source describes multiblock modeling as combining multiple data sources from the same sample into a contiguous data set, with UV-vis, NIR, and Raman spectra combined into fused spectral matrices.
items.how_it_applies: This supports testing a fused matrix approach for multiple spectroscopy methods, while keeping the same-sample requirement in mind when aligning NIR and MIR data.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The work is on lanthanide solutions in a PMMA microfluidic device, not dairy whey or an in-line flow cell, so the fusion benefit may not transfer to protein concentration in a turbid stream.

citation.quote: Multiblock modeling involves combining multiple sources of data measured from the same sample into a contiguous data set.36 In this case, UV-vis, NIR, and Raman spectra were combined to form fused spectral matrices.
citation.label: E04 ¶46

items.finding: The source reports that mid-level data fusion outperformed low-level data fusion for rapid quality detection of wheat flour.
items.how_it_applies: This could inform the fusion strategy by suggesting that a joined, block-scaled matrix (low-level) should be compared against mid-level fusion rather than assumed best.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The result is from wheat flour quality detection, not dairy whey, and it does not test NIR and MIR at a shared flow-cell location or normalisation to a common time step.

citation.quote: The results indicated that mid-level data fusion outperformed low-level data fusion, providing an effective solution for the rapid quality detection of wheat flour (Zareef et al., 2023) (Fig. 4C).
citation.label: E05 ¶25

items.finding: The source states that one model can quantify spectra from all pathlengths despite significant differences in measurement conditions at multiple physical locations.
items.how_it_applies: This could inform the premise by suggesting a single robust model be tested across clear and more turbid states, with attention to whether turbidity acts like a pathlength or scattering change.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a microfluidic study with lanthanide solutions and varying optical pathlengths, not dairy whey or turbidity, so the transfer to a clear/turbid stream state is uncertain.

citation.quote: The goal of quantifying spectra from all pathlengths using one model is to allow for simultaneous measurement and quantification of solutions at multiple physical locations in a system despite significant differences in the measurement conditions at those locations.
citation.label: E04 ¶42
